query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of chromium (Cr) to a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) can improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) in its as-cast or as-fabricated state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of chromium (Cr) to the RHEA
generation.conditions: High-temperature environment (above 1000°C) in the presence of oxygen
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Cr-rich oxide layer on the surface of the RHEA
generation.mechanism: The added Cr reacts with oxygen to form a protective Cr-rich oxide layer, which reduces the oxidation rate of the RHEA
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance of the RHEA, resulting in reduced oxidation and improved mechanical properties
generation.baseline: The oxidation rate of the RHEA without the added Cr
generation.boundary: The temperature range above 1000°C, where the Cr-rich oxide layer is stable and effective in reducing oxidation
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Cr to be added, the effect of other alloying elements on the oxidation resistance, and the long-term stability of the Cr-rich oxide layer

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate of the RHEA with added Cr is not significantly lower than that of the RHEA without added Cr, then the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Abstract WVTaTiCr x ( x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings were prepared on a 42-CrMo steel plate using laser cladding. The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. As the temperature capability of modern Ni- based superalloys has reached its limit for gas turbine engine applications, materials scientists are searching for new materials with higher temperature capabilities. Recently, “High-Entropy Alloy (HEA)” [1] , [2] has been proposed as a new strategy for alloy design with a wide composition space. Other names such as “compositionally complex alloys (CCAs)” has also been given to this class of alloy containing multiple phases [3] . Nevertheless, the alloy design strategy of HEA/CCA shows great promise for exploring new alloy systems. RHEA was first proposed by Senkov et al . [4] as an attempt to create new alloy systems for high temperature applications beyond superalloys. Abstract A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method. The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail. The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina. With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material. Keywords: high entropy alloys, metal matrix composites, mechanical properties
